title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 104
paragraphs: To this Demaratus replied: “O king, from the first I was sure that if I told the truth, I would not be speaking anything pleasing to you. But since you compelled me to speak the very truth, I told you about the affairs of the Spartans. Yet you know better than anyone how I am at this present time affectionately disposed toward them — seeing that they first stripped me of the rank and privileges inherited from my fathers, and then made me a stateless exile. Your father took me in, gave me a livelihood and a house to live in. It is surely not reasonable to suppose that a prudent man would push aside the friendliness offered to him; rather he would accept it gratefully. I do not profess that I can fight ten men, or even two; if I had my choice, I would not even fight one. But if there were necessity, or some great cause pressing me into combat, I would most willingly fight one of those men who claim each to be a match for three Greeks. So too the Lacedaemonians, one against one, are inferior to no men, and in a body they are the best of all. For though they are free, they are not free in all things: over them is set Law as their master, whom they fear far more than your people fear you. At any rate, whatever their master commands, they do; and he commands always the same thing — he forbids them to flee out of battle before any multitude of men, but orders them to stay at their post and either win the victory or lose their life. If I seem to you to be speaking foolishly in saying these things, I prefer from now on to be silent about the rest; I spoke now only because I was forced. May it nevertheless turn out as you wish, O king.”
